Real-world lecanemab PET monitoring reveals visual-quantitative discordance

In 38 amyloid-PET-positive patients treated for 6–8 months, amyloid burden fell by 29.39±22.31 Centiloids, but visual and quantitative response agreement was poor to fair (κ 0.205–0.253), supporting explicit Centiloid quantification for serial monitoring rather than visual interpretation alone.

Real-world lecanemab PET monitoring reveals visual-quantitative discordance

In 38 amyloid-PET-positive patients treated for 6–8 months, amyloid burden fell by 29.39±22.31 Centiloids, but visual and quantitative response agreement was poor to fair (κ 0.205–0.253), supporting explicit Centiloid quantification for serial monitoring rather than visual interpretation alone.

Key quantitative results: Mean amyloid reduction was 29.39±22.31 Centiloids (p<0.001); MMSE, MoCA and tau-PET measures did not change significantly.

BiomarkersAmyloid PETAmyloid CentiloidTau PET SUVRTreatment response monitoring

Added October 16, 2026 · DOI:10.1177/13872877261493063

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The cohort shows substantial short-term plaque reduction without measurable cognitive or tau-PET change. Only 12 of 38 reached less than 24.1 Centiloids and five were visually negative. The discordance supports quantitative serial assessment when PET is obtained, but this small uncontrolled cohort cannot prove clinical utility or determine when treatment should stop.

Study design

Investigators retrospectively analyzed 38 amyloid-PET-positive patients with Alzheimer disease who received lecanemab for 6–8 months. Paired tests evaluated Centiloid and cognitive change, kappa measured visual-quantitative agreement, and exploratory regression assessed predictors of amyloid reduction.

Key quantitative results

  • Mean amyloid reduction was 29.39±22.31 Centiloids (p<0.001); MMSE, MoCA and tau-PET measures did not change significantly.
  • Twelve of 38 patients reached less than 24.1 Centiloids, while only five were visually negative.
  • Visual-quantitative agreement was poor to fair: κ=0.205 for positivity and κ=0.253 for treatment efficacy.
  • Baseline Centiloid burden (standardized β=0.594, p<0.001) and number of treatment cycles (β=0.285, p=0.022) independently predicted greater clearance; tau SUVR had a marginal inverse association (β=-0.238, p=0.052). The multivariable model adjusted R² was 0.507.

What changed

This real-world study directly quantifies the gap between visual and Centiloid-based interpretation during short-term lecanemab therapy and proposes a hybrid screening-and-monitoring workflow.

Strength of evidence

Early real-world evidence with paired PET and quantitative effect estimates, but retrospective, uncontrolled and limited to 38 patients. Visual-reading methods, tracer/scanner generalizability and downstream clinical utility require independent validation.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

If serial amyloid PET is obtained, visual negativity alone may miss low residual burden and quantitative Centiloid reporting can add interpretive precision. The study does not establish that routine serial PET improves outcomes or should guide dose changes.

Field medical relevance

Addresses recurring MSL questions about visual versus quantitative reads, low-burden discordance, Centiloid thresholds and PET-based response monitoring under anti-amyloid therapy.

Quanterix or platform relevance

The central comparison is visual versus quantitative amyloid-PET interpretation during lecanemab treatment. Poor agreement indicates that visual and Centiloid assessments are not interchangeable near low residual burden; the study did not validate performance across tracers, scanners or independent readers.

Access or reimbursement relevance

No authorization or coverage change. Serial quantitative PET could increase imaging demand and cost; the study did not evaluate reimbursement or access.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does the study establish routine serial PET monitoring?
No. It shows measurement discordance in a small cohort but did not test whether serial PET improves treatment decisions or outcomes.
Can visual negativity and less than 24.1 Centiloids be treated as equivalent?
No. Twelve patients crossed the quantitative threshold while only five were visually negative, and kappa agreement was low.
Did plaque reduction produce short-term cognitive improvement?
No significant MMSE or MoCA change was detected over 6–8 months.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Historical criteria-repair backfill rather than a newly published item
  • Retrospective single-cohort design
  • Only 38 patients
  • No untreated comparator
  • Short 6–8-month follow-up
  • No validation across tracers, scanners or independent readers
  • No clinical-utility or patient-outcome analysis

Primary source · DOI

Qiao Z, Zhao X, Wang G, et al. PET-based evaluation of short-term amyloid-β clearance and predictive factors in real-world Alzheimer's disease patients treated with lecanemab. J Alzheimers Dis. Published online October 8, 2026. doi:10.1177/13872877261493063.
